hook_text: Three threads, one exam. Here is the whole of Term 2 Technology in sixty seconds.
clip_script: Thread one, developments: draw the base, hang the four sides, hang the lid off the back, add glue flaps. Dashed folds, solid cuts, six faces, matching edges. Open tray is a cross; prism is three rectangles and two triangles. Thread two, forces: ask what the load is doing to the part. Chain pulled, tension. Seat across a span, bending. Spindle turned, torsion. Steel goes where concrete is pulled, bottom of a beam, top over a column. Plywood crosses its layers. I-beam for bending, tubes for squashing and twisting. Thread three, impact: name the material, one good, one bad with its life stage, one fix. Polystyrene keeps food hot; it sits in drains for decades; paperboard with a return crate. Read the command word, draw with a ruler, write both sides, leave nothing blank.
visual_style: Whiteboard splits into three columns; a box unfolds into a labelled net; a swing and bicycle light up part by part with force names; a three-sentence paragraph types itself with good, bad and fix highlighted.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the net of a lidded box from memory, then check it has six faces.
